title: Kev answers preserve benchmark inputs and replayable records
description:
Feature: Kev participates in the shared benchmark
Scenario: Answer a task without changing its experiment
Given a task with committed text, ordered options, and a pinned Kev deployment
When Kev answers the task
Then each question and option retains its committed meaning and order
And the answer includes validated probabilities and model provenance
Scenario: Resume interrupted collection
Given compatible completed and partial Kev records
When collection resumes
Then completed items are not requested again and incompatible inputs or model versions are refused
Scenario: Add new coverage
Given a newly registered task and cue with committed stimuli
When the runner plans Kev collection
Then the task is discovered from the shared task definitions without a Kev-specific task list
Scenario: Replay offline
Given a committed Kev answer record
When the scorer and report run without a server
Then the Kev result is reproduced and missing cells remain missing

comments.author: home
comments.text: Additional execution specification before implementation: Feature: frozen Kev study execution. Scenario: reject changed inputs. Given a committed coverage manifest, when any listed input hash or planned cell count differs, then fail before an engine answers. Scenario: retained timing pilot. Given the committed surgeon-physician item order, when pilot runs, then send exactly the first 20 original test bios, retain every response with pinned provenance and elapsed time in studies/kev/pilot.jsonl, and mark these as separate calls repeated by normal collection. Scenario: complete coverage. Given matching frozen files and provenance, when study collection runs, then collect each listed cell in manifest order with option-order mapped to option-order-reversed, preserving normal collector resume checks. Scenario: offline planning. Given no engine endpoint, when dry-run runs, then validate hashes and counts without any network requests. Pilot answers never select or modify the model or study population.
